label: final copy step of short (L=3) sequences, plus L=4 recall-2 on t/p
explanation: Very weak unit (max 0.012) that fires only in the copy phase, never on original-token or delimiter steps, and never on a first occurrence of the input token. About 55% of activation mass falls on L=3 sequences, mostly at the last copy step (t=5, recall_idx=2, where the input is the fed-back orig(1)). Another big piece is L=4 at recall_idx=2. Magnitude depends on the input token: t and p give the strongest activations (all top examples are L=3, t=5, with input t, p or q), and inputs like a/e/u/h rarely fire. The rest is a thin tail of low-activation firing on t/p inputs near the end of longer sequences (to_go<=1, e.g. L=9 t=16-17). The predicate gets dev F1 0.45 and mass recall 0.65. Precision is limited because many L=3 and L=4 final steps with other input tokens do not fire.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=6: p, t, 2, q; t=10: t, y, p, k; t=11: t, y, p, g) and the previous input (most: z, 1, 3, p, j, l; least: d, w, h, o); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, L=3 & t=5, L=4 & t=6.
